definition: Abnegation means the denial of comforts or pleasures to oneself.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abnegation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abnegation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: His abnegation puzzled the heirs: a fortune in the bank, yet he walked, mended his coats, and went without.

Restraint is far milder than abnegation — a single no, declining the second slice, skipping one sale — and it costs you an evening at most, while abnegation strings those refusals into a whole chosen season of bare living.
Martyrdom goes further than abnegation — abnegation gives up comforts; martyrdom gives up the whole self, and does not come back from it.

Self-denial is the everyday word for refusing yourself pleasures — skipping dessert, passing on a purchase — and it can be casual, small, or brief. Abnegation is the graver, more deliberate practice: comforts given up in a sustained way, usually for a vow, a goal, or a principle with moral weight.

Going without is the plainest phrase for lacking something, and it says nothing about why — you can go without because the money ran out. Abnegation adds the choosing: you impose the lack on yourself, on purpose and for a purpose, which is what gives the word its moral weight.
